what_it_does: This paper addresses retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), a technique where large language models (LLMs) answer questions by first retrieving relevant documents from a knowledge base, then generating an answer conditioned on those documents. RAG systems face two distinct bottlenecks: the retrieval phase accesses memory in unpredictable patterns with low bandwidth efficiency, while the generation phase requires many matrix-vector multiplications over gigabytes of LLM weights. The paper proposes using two complementary memory technologies: high-bandwidth memory (HBM) with processing-in-memory (PIM) capabilities for the bandwidth-hungry generation phase, and cheaper dual-in-line-memory-module (DIMM) based PIM for the capacity-hungry knowledge base and irregular retrieval accesses.
